health_utility.response_aggregation: 0.7 * worst response value + 0.3 * mean response value across attack/evasive policies
health_utility.boundary: Health utility is antisymmetric under side swap for the same outcome. Total search retains positional, timing, wait and friendly-fire heuristics. This finite response ensemble is not an exhaustive minimax/Nash solution or calibrated win probability.

application_changes: Both sides use the same relative health payoff and response aggregation.
Progress-triggered forced attacks must preserve the best risk-adjusted health exchange, rather than categorically maximizing own survivor count.
Ready attacks may accept own losses when the joint outcome is favorable; victory/defeat/mutual elimination remain explicit.
Material changes in approved route health advantage (>12 points) or either side's living count suspend continuation for reassessment.
Model descriptions use ally/enemy aliases instead of Blue/Red IDs; actual plan mappings remain intact in diagnostics.
Existing v4 persistence, low-level safety checks and historical v1-v4 protocols remain separately supported.

live_fixed_state_checks.observed_ahead: Both checkpoints, both sides: two immediate firing orders, press_advantage. The progress/exchange gate left a single candidate in these four calls; this is application selection, not evidence of model strategy skill.
live_fixed_state_checks.observed_behind: Both checkpoints, both sides: mirrored repositioning orders, balanced exchange instead of forcing unfavorable mutual damage.
live_fixed_state_checks.boundary: Eight fixed-state inference/readout checks with generated asymmetric health inputs, not completed battles, independent accuracy labels, learned-score symmetry or evidence of optimal tactics.

adapter_checks: Injected transport/parser tests cover both sides through NanoJev Boolean, Laya Noul and CLI 0..100 self-preferences. The same planner readout is used; native gates, raw Noul metadata and CLI self-scores keep distinct provenance.
privacy: Synthetic aggregate only. Full fixed-state requests/responses remain in private local research receipts; no credentials published.
